result:
Understood, and thanks for the patience. I'll keep this short. One decision is left before I write: how it fits with what's already running. The taproom tabs app is a small Flask app with SQLite on the office Pi. There are two real ways to build on that:

**1. Add batch tracking to the existing taproom app (my pick).**
New pages for mash day, opening a sack (scan the lot number), and the bottling run that sends labels to the printer. The data goes in its own tables in the same database. It's one app, one Pi and one thing to back up. The trade-off is that a bug in batch tracking could, in the worst case, take down tabs. I'd keep the batch code walled off in its own section of the app to limit that.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi, with its own database.**
Brewing and the taproom can't break each other. The cost is two apps to start, update and back up, and any shared details, like beer names, would live in two places.

I'm dropping off-the-shelf brewery software. You've described something specific, and you already have a working app to build on.

I recommend option 1, because it's the least to look after on one Pi.

This is a project-sized piece, so once you pick, I'll write the full design and save it to the project. A reviewer will read it before you do, and I may come back once with a few questions from that. Which way do you want to go?
